title: Recomputed low-isotope mass table after the q-Hecke character gap closure (proton, neutron, D, T, ³He)
html:
Recomputed low-isotope mass table

Following the q-Hecke character closure (Partition-sum form of \mathrm{tr}_M) and the \rho_K refinement, three independent production paths to the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K) at q = q_0 agree to the 60-digit serialization floor (relative residual \lesssim 10^{-49}) across the proton, neutron, deuteron, tritium, and {}^{3}\mathrm{He}. Both tabulated paths evaluate z = q^3/(q^2+1) on the Borromean word at the proton-anchored q_0, certifying the character closure directly.

Cross-check

See Table 1.

Direct binding formulation

The atomic-mass formula is:

  \mathfrak{m}(K) = (Z m_p + N m_n) + \mathrm{Binding}(K), \qquad
  \mathrm{Binding}(K) = m_e \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3A} y_\lambda(q) \chi^\lambda(\mathcal{B}_K) \Delta_\lambda(K).

This direct form supersedes the equivalent factorisation \mathfrak{m}(K) = \rho_K m_e |\mathrm{tr}_M(K)|, where \rho_K = \rho_K^{\mathrm{LO}} + (\Sigma_\lambda y_\lambda \chi^\lambda \Delta_\lambda)/|\mathrm{tr}_M|. In the factorisation, the leading-order term \rho_K^{\mathrm{LO}} = (Z m_p + N m_n)/(m_e |\mathrm{tr}_M|) forces the |\mathrm{tr}_M| factor to cancel identically against the outer multiplier, recovering the constituent mass Z m_p + N m_n. While \rho_K packages constituent and binding masses into a single symbol, the sole physical content resides in the \Delta_\lambda correction. One therefore writes the constituent sum and binding terms side by side.

Calibrated form

One presents the calibrated form, where \rho_K^{\mathrm{LO}} consumes CODATA m_p and m_n as upstream inputs. This violates the three-calibration discipline by injecting m_p and m_n as extraneous calibration constants. The proton and neutron rows are tautological by construction.

See Table 2.

† Proton and neutron predictions equal CODATA exactly because m_p and m_n are upstream inputs in this leading-order form. A 0.000\% relative error here represents a calibration tautology, not prediction quality.

Full \mathfrak{Q}_\beta prediction

The framework predicts the \beta-decay Q-value using only the electron mass (CAL-1) and the substrate parameter q_0 (CAL-2) (Symbolic Q-value of free neutron decay). One injects no CODATA nucleon masses and does not use \mathfrak{Q}_\beta as an input. Rather, \mathfrak{Q}_\beta becomes an output.

Evaluating the single-wrap difference \Delta via the Markov trace at z = q_0^3/(q_0^2+1), with the order-zero scale E_0 = m_e/(q_0(q_0-1)), gives:

\boxed{
\mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\Delta} =
\Bigl|\tfrac{h^2}{2} - h\,z\Bigr|\,E_0
\approx 0.4447 \text{ MeV}
}

This yields a -43.16\% residual (-337.6 keV) against the CODATA value of 0.7823 MeV. No c_k precision ladder has yet been derived at z = q^3/(q^2+1), so the residual is reported directly. With the tower-summed E_0 the value is 0.4491 MeV (-42.59\%). The scored \mathfrak{Q}_\beta applies the T^3 weight split of the z = q_0^3/(q_0^2+1) trace to the \gamma\gamma base V^3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3, giving \mathfrak{Q}_\beta \approx 0.3254 MeV (-58.40\%) (Symbolic Q-value of free neutron decay); the \Delta trace above is retained as an unscored comparison.

The \Delta expression comes from the symbolic normal-form difference between the single-wrap proton (L_+ - \tfrac{h}{2}\sigma_0) and neutron (L_+ - h\sigma_0 - \tfrac{h}{2}\sigma_1 + \tfrac{h^2}{2}\gamma), namely \Delta = \tfrac{h^2}{2}\gamma - \tfrac{h}{2}\sigma_0 - \tfrac{h}{2}\sigma_1 with h = q_0 - q_0^{-1}. The Markov trace sends \gamma \mapsto 1 and each \sigma_i \mapsto z, giving h^2/2 - h z, multiplied by E_0 = m_e/(q_0(q_0-1)); at single wrap, the L_+, L_-, and e^- contributions cancel.

Coordinate-sum Form A (z = 1 comparison). Weighting every basis element by 1 instead gives \Delta(\mathrm{net}) = h(h-2)/2 and m_e |q_0^2 - 2q_0 - 1| (q_0 + 1)/(2 q_0^3) \approx 0.7836 MeV (+0.168\%). That weighting corresponds to z = 1, which does not satisfy the two-row Markov faithfulness condition y_{(1^3)}(z) = 0; it is retained for algebraic comparison only.

See Table 3.

Single-wrap symbolic versus typed-crossings 6-term form

The typed-crossings 6-term decomposition (Energy scale of the Hecke normal form) has |\Delta(\mathrm{net})| = 0.18829 and yields \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{(\text{6-term})} = 0.7882 MeV (+0.747\%). The single-wrap form is tighter by a factor of 4.46. The L_\pm and e^- contributions vanish exactly in the symbolic single-wrap difference, but pick up small asymmetric finite-size contributions in the typed-crossings basis. Both of these are Form A (weight-1) evaluations and are retired with it; the typed-crossings form remains in the witness solely for cross-checking.

Basis dependence

The decomposition into observable (\ell \ge 2) versus virtual (\ell < 2) sectors by Coxeter length is only meaningful in the typed-crossings 6-term basis, where it yields a 58.46\% / 41.54\% split. At single wrap, all \ell \ge 2 channels cancel because the proton and neutron share identical Hopf content. The entire single-wrap Q-value lives in the virtual sector. This poses no contradiction: the typed-crossings basis is finer, and its observable share reflects finite-size and multi-wrap structures absent from the single-wrap closed form.

Performance summary

See Table 4.

Categorical verification of the proton pole order

  \mathrm{ord}_{u=0}\bigl(\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_p)\bigr) = 19 = 18 Z + 21 N + 1 \quad \text{at } (Z, N) = (1, 0).
  \mathrm{ord}_{u=0}\bigl(\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_D)\bigr) = 40 = 18 (1) + 21 (1) + 1.

These orders are rigorously exact, as lower-order poles cannot cancel a strict maximum. This closes the multi-nucleon case. The coefficient 18 is the per-proton additive contribution to the summed u-pole order. It is not the q-pole order of any individual representation (the maximum per-irrep order at H_3 is 11 for \lambda = (2, 1)).
